strapline: Twenty honours at State House, a budget date for Friday, the 48-hour rule on the opposition's lips — and Nkana's run ends at Konkola

stories.title: Twenty names at State House: a crocodile rescue, the Chalala hero and the Trade Kings founder lead the Independence honours, with Kanyemba and the late Melu recognised for sport
stories.excerpt: President Hakainde Hichilema decorated 20 people at an investiture ceremony at State House on Saturday 24 October, the 62nd anniversary of independence. The Times of Zambia's list runs from freedom fighters to a fisherman who pulled a colleague from a crocodile, Robby Chitambo, who helped police find 13 abducted young women in Chalala in 2022, and Trade Kings' Iqbal Patel. Copper Princesses coach Carol Kanyemba received the President's Insignia of Meritorious Achievement.

image.label: The 62nd investiture
image.caption: Twenty people were honoured at State House on Saturday 24 October 2026 as part of the 62nd independence anniversary.

body: Zambia's 62nd Independence Day was marked on Saturday 24 October with events in all ten provinces and, at State House in Lusaka, with the annual investiture at which the President confers national honours. According to the Times of Zambia, President Hakainde Hichilema decorated 20 people for acts of courage, sacrifice and contributions to national development. News Diggers reported that the ceremonies across the country took place in intense October heat that drew complaints from many of those who turned out.

The Times of Zambia's account gives the fullest list of recipients. Among those honoured for bravery were Robby Chitambo, recognised for helping to rescue 13 young women abducted in Lusaka in 2022, and Newton Nalumilo, a fisherman who saved a fellow fisherman from a crocodile attack. The Zambian Observer reported that Chitambo received the Gallantry Medal: in 2022 he was a civilian who helped the authorities locate the captives in the Chalala area, and he has since been employed by the Zambia Air Force. News Diggers described the case as the abduction of mobile money agent Pamela Chisumpa and twelve other young women.

body.text: Business, law, education and the liberation struggle

body: Business was represented by Iqbal Patel, whom the Times of Zambia describes as founder and chairman of Trade Kings, with investments it says have created more than 16,000 jobs, and by Yaochi Huang, proprietor of the Wonderful Group. News Diggers' headline referred to the two as the Trade Kings boss and a Chinese investor. Patel told the Times that the recognition would motivate the company to keep supplying quality products.

body.text: This recognition by the President is a motivation.
body.attribution: Iqbal Patel, Trade Kings, speaking after the investiture at State House on Saturday 24 October, as reported by the Times of Zambia

body: The late Ambassador Cox Sikumba was honoured for peacekeeping work in Mozambique. His widow, Naomi Sikumba, told the Times of Zambia that the honour meant a great deal to the family, noting that he died in the 1986 plane crash that also killed the Mozambican president, Samora Machel. From the independence struggle the Times lists Timothy Hakalinda, who lost his left eye during the liberation fight, and Mwewa Chibwe, Rabson Chibululu and Saul Mambepa, recognised for their efforts to restrict the movement of colonialists. Professor Chalo Bayeyani and Dr George Lipimile were honoured for contributions to international law, Veronica Kunda for her work as a firefighting instructor, Dr Michael Chilala for education reform and digital development, Mr and Mrs Sharadchandra Desai jointly for education, healthcare and community work, Mubmwae Smith for education and youth empowerment, and Joseph Daka for agricultural development.

body.text: Three from sport

body: Three sporting figures were decorated. The Zambian Observer reported that boxer Patrick Chinyemba, who fought for Zambia at the Commonwealth Games and the Paris Olympics, was recognised for his amateur career; that Carol Kanyemba, head coach of the Under-17 women's team, was honoured for youth development and women's football; and that the late Ashios Melu, a former national captain and coach, was honoured posthumously. ZamFoot, citing confirmation from the Football Association of Zambia, reported that Kanyemba received the President's Insignia of Meritorious Achievement. A Zambia Army officer and first assistant coach at Green Buffaloes Women, she is the first Zambian woman to coach a national side at a FIFA World Cup and the first Zambian coach of either sex to take a team to three consecutive World Cups: the Under-17 women's tournaments of 2024, 2025 and 2026.

body.text: I'm so honoured and so blessed for the recognition.
body.attribution: Carol Kanyemba, Copper Princesses head coach, after the investiture on Saturday 24 October, as reported by ZamFoot

body: News Diggers also reported that King Charles III sent Independence Day wishes reaffirming the relationship between the United Kingdom and Zambia, and that the President, in his anniversary message, called the 62nd anniversary a reminder that building the nation is everyone's responsibility, urging citizens to unite and work hard. Lusaka Brief reported his full Independence message, and the opposition's response to it, on Sunday 25 October.

body.title: The honours list as reported by the Times of Zambia
items: Bravery: Robby Chitambo (Chalala rescue, 2022); Newton Nalumilo (crocodile rescue)
Business: Iqbal Patel (Trade Kings); Yaochi Huang (Wonderful Group); Joseph Daka (agriculture)
Liberation struggle: Timothy Hakalinda; Mwewa Chibwe; Rabson Chibululu; Saul Mambepa
Public service and the professions: the late Ambassador Cox Sikumba; Prof Chalo Bayeyani; Dr George Lipimile; Veronica Kunda; Dr Michael Chilala; Mr and Mrs Sharadchandra Desai; Mubmwae Smith
Sport: Patrick Chinyemba (boxing); Carol Kanyemba (football); the late Ashios Melu (football)

body.confirmed: That 20 people were honoured at State House on Saturday 24 October is reported by the Times of Zambia, and the Saturday date and venue are confirmed by the Zambian Observer and ZamFoot. The names above are the Times of Zambia's list; Chitambo's Gallantry Medal is reported by the Zambian Observer and Kanyemba's Insignia by ZamFoot, citing FAZ.
body.unverified: The grade of honour conferred on most recipients was not given in the pages read. Spellings differ between outlets: News Diggers calls the rescuer Robert Chitambo and the Trade Kings founder Mohamed Igbal Patel, while the Times of Zambia uses Robby Chitambo and Iqbal Patel; News Diggers calls Patel a co-founder and the Times the founder and chairman. The full citations read at the ceremony have not been published by the outlets cited.

stories.title: 'Not a mere procedural formality': M'membe says the 48-hour rule is being ignored after the August election, while Mweetwa tells the House the vote passed without violence
stories.excerpt: The Socialist Party used the Independence weekend to press two arguments. In a statement on Sunday 25 October, Fred M'membe said opposition figures and critics are being held beyond the constitutional 48 hours without charge, and called for it to stop. General secretary Cosmas Musumali called President Hichilema's COMESA role an opening for economic diplomacy but said he has not yet matured into an African leader. In Parliament, UPND's Cornelius Mweetwa said August saw no violence beyond the chaos after Brian Mundubile declared himself president-elect.

image.label: The 48-hour rule
image.caption: The Socialist Party says suspects are being held beyond the constitutional 48 hours; the ruling party says the August election was peaceful.

body: The Socialist Party's answer to the Independence weekend came in two parts. On Sunday 25 October its president, Dr Fred M'membe, issued a statement in Lusaka condemning what he called the prolonged detention of opposition figures and government critics since the general election of 13 August. According to Zambia Monitor and the Zambian Observer, which both carried the statement, M'membe said Zambia could not describe itself as peaceful while constitutionalism, due process and the rule of law were being undermined, and that holding people beyond the 48 hours the Constitution allows, without a formal charge or a court appearance, raised serious questions about citizens' fundamental rights.

body.text: The 48-hour rule is not a mere procedural formality.
body.attribution: Dr Fred M'membe, Socialist Party president, statement issued in Lusaka on Sunday 25 October, as carried by the Zambian Observer

body: M'membe described the rule as a safeguard against arbitrary state power and warned that detention without judicial oversight could create fear and instability and erode public confidence in law enforcement. He called on the Government and the police to halt what he termed arbitrary and prolonged detentions at once, and argued that an independent judiciary and a separation of powers were needed to keep the executive accountable. The Zambian Observer quoted him adding that the exercise of power must be a constant practice of self-limitation and modesty.

The statement did not, as reported, name the people it had in mind. Zambia Monitor's weekly round-up of Saturday 24 October gives some of the background: the State has denied violating the constitutional rights of Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others accused of treason, arguing that the cases are complex and need extensive investigation, and Lima MP Kelvin Kaunda applied for bail pending trial on an assault charge after five days in police custody.

body.text: COMESA and the measure of a leader

body: The party's general secretary, Dr Cosmas Musumali, took a different line of attack in an interview on Friday 23 October reported by News Diggers and the Zambian Observer. Musumali said the election of President Hakainde Hichilema as vice-chairperson of COMESA on Thursday, alongside Zimbabwe's Emmerson Mnangagwa as chairperson, was an opportunity for Zambia to raise its economic diplomacy. But he said the President had not yet matured into an African leader, because he had at times taken a contrary position on issues where most African countries held a different view.

The Government's reading of the same appointment was given in Parliament last week. Replying to Itezhi-Tezhi East MP Credo Nanjuwa during the Vice-President's Question Time, Vice-President Mutale Nalumango said the COMESA vice-chairmanship gave Zambia a chance to expand trade with member states and find markets for locally produced goods in a regional market of more than 680 million people, complementing the African Continental Free Trade Area and the Grow Zambia Agenda, the Times of Zambia reported.

body.text: 'The best speech in 16 years'

body: The ruling party's account of the post-election period is sharply different from M'membe's. Debating the President's address to the first session of the 14th National Assembly on Thursday 22 October, Choma Central UPND MP Cornelius Mweetwa said no violence was recorded during the August elections apart from the chaos that followed Brian Mundubile's declaration that he had won the presidency, News Diggers reported. Mweetwa called the President's speech the best he had heard in 16 years and said it was soothing to hear him reaffirm his commitment to democracy.

The police, for their part, have promised even-handedness in the next test. In a statement on Saturday 24 October reported by Zambia Monitor, Inspector General of Police Graphael Musamba said officers would act firmly and impartially against anyone breaking the law before the Mandevu by-election on 5 November, regardless of party, and that an alleged assault on suspected members of a political party in the constituency on 22 October would be investigated.

stories.title: Home from a job that was not the job: two Zambian women repatriated from India over alleged exploitation, as Immigration removes 193 foreign nationals in a single day
stories.excerpt: The Department of Immigration said on Saturday 24 October that two Zambian women who went to India for work in July ended up in different work from what they had agreed, took refuge at the Zambian Embassy and were flown home, arriving at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport on 15 October. The same statement reported the removal of 193 foreign nationals from Lusaka on Thursday 22 October, most of them Burundians, and a Zambian deported from Dubai. Spokesman Namati Nshinka urged job-seekers to verify agents and contracts before travelling.

image.label: Two returns, 193 removals
image.caption: The Department of Immigration's weekend statement covered a repatriation from India, a deportation from Dubai and a mass removal from Lusaka.

body: Two Zambian women have been brought home from India after what the Department of Immigration describes as allegations of labour and sexual exploitation. The department's chief public relations officer, Namati Nshinka, set out the case in a statement issued in Lusaka on Saturday 24 October and reported by Zambia Monitor, News Diggers and the Zambian Observer.

According to the statement, the two women travelled to India in July 2026 for employment but found themselves doing work different from what had been agreed. They sought refuge at the Zambian Embassy, which arranged their return. Immigration officers received them at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport, News Diggers giving the date as Thursday 15 October, and handed them to officers from the Department of Social Welfare and the Anti-Human Trafficking Department. The department has not named the women, and nothing in the statement as reported indicates that anyone has been charged in connection with their treatment. News Diggers' headline described the case as sex trafficking; the department's own wording, as quoted by all three outlets, refers to allegations of labour and sexual exploitation.

body.text: A technician from Dubai, and 193 removals

body: Zambia Monitor reported that on the same day the department received a Zambian man deported from Dubai for unlawful stay. He had left Zambia on 29 March 2026 and, according to the statement, had been working as a technician at Amazon. The Zambian Observer described him as having overstayed his authorised visit.

The statement also disclosed a large removal operation. On Thursday 22 October the Department of Immigration in Lusaka removed 193 foreign nationals: 164 Burundians, 22 Tanzanians, four Rwandans and three Ugandans. Some had been convicted of immigration offences and had paid court-imposed fines; the others were removed administratively, Zambia Monitor and the Zambian Observer reported.

body.text: The department's advice

body: Nshinka used the statement to warn Zambians looking for work abroad to exercise due diligence, particularly with recruitment agents whose credentials cannot be verified. Prospective migrant workers were urged to obtain clearance from the Ministry of Labour and Social Security and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, and to check the employer, the contract and the destination country's immigration requirements before leaving, so as to avoid exploitation and trafficking.

stories.title: Budget day is Friday: Musokotwane to present the 2027 estimates on 30 October, after which the House breaks for ten working days of sector scrutiny
stories.excerpt: Vice-President Mutale Nalumango told the National Assembly on Friday 23 October that Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane will present the 2027 National Budget on Friday 30 October, News Diggers reports. The Speaker will then suspend the business of the House for ten working days so that sector budgets can be analysed, with the House resuming on 24 November. The budget follows a K19.9 billion supplementary request dominated by maize payments, and a World Bank pledge to back the 2027 fiscal programme.

image.label: Friday 30 October
image.caption: The 2027 National Budget is to be presented on Friday 30 October 2026, according to the Vice-President's business statement.

body: The date of the 2027 National Budget has been set. In her business statement to the National Assembly on Friday 23 October, Vice-President Mutale Nalumango announced that the Minister of Finance and National Planning, Dr Situmbeko Musokotwane, will present the budget on Friday 30 October, News Diggers reported on Saturday 24 October.

The same report set out the timetable that follows. Within seven days of the presentation, Speaker Nelly Mutti will suspend the business of the House for ten working days so that MPs can analyse the sector budgets, and the House is due to resume on 24 November alongside the work of the Expanded Budget Committee. To clear the way, Nalumango said she would move a motion on Thursday 29 October to suspend certain Standing Orders, among them Standing Order 25, so that the House can sit from 14:15 on Friday 30 October until the day's business is concluded.

body.text: The exchange over the Cabinet

body: That the budget was coming within the week had already surfaced in the chamber. The Zambian Observer reported that on Friday 23 October Shiwang'andu MP Stephen Kampyongo asked how a budget due for presentation the following week could be defended if a complete Cabinet was not yet in place. Nalumango rejected the premise, saying the executive was intact, structurally sound and ready to steer the State's financial plan through the House, and that the Cabinet was fully functional and not a product of opposition dreams.

body.text: What the budget follows

body: The 2027 estimates arrive on top of a second supplementary budget for 2026. Last week Musokotwane asked the House for K19.9 billion, the Zambia Daily Mail reported on Friday 23 October, with K14.7 billion of it to pay farmers who supplied maize to the Food Reserve Agency, which bought 2.7 million tonnes against a target of 500,000 tonnes. The Ministry of Agriculture takes K15.8 billion, or 79 per cent, including K1.1 billion for the 2026/27 Farmer Input Support Programme e-voucher. The rest covers K1.3 billion for the Ministry of Finance, K540 million for student loans and scholarships through HELSB, K422.5 million for the Ministry of Defence and a K300 million contingency. The supplementary is to be financed mainly by K18 billion of domestic borrowing, with K1.3 billion in extra revenue, K510.8 million in additional donor funding and smaller savings. The Speaker referred the estimates to the expanded Planning and Budgeting Committee.

External backing was signalled the same week. News Diggers reported on Friday 23 October that the World Bank, in a statement from the Office of the Secretary to the Treasury, had committed to supporting Zambia's 2027 fiscal programme through a Development Policy Operation, and that its vice-president for Eastern and Southern Africa, Ndiame Diop, had indicated willingness to support the rehabilitation of the northern railway circuit, the Agri-Connect project and a proposed skills enhancement project.

stories.title: Two-thirds of the way: 675,459 farmers have redeemed their FISP inputs, and the Ministry tells agro-dealers to keep the shelves stocked as the El Niño advisories go out
stories.excerpt: The Ministry of Agriculture said on Saturday 24 October that 675,459 farmers had redeemed inputs under the 2026/27 Farmer Input Support Programme by 23 October, 65.93 per cent of the 1,024,434 targeted beneficiaries and ahead of the pace at the same point last year. Spokesman Balewa Zyuulu urged agro-dealers to keep enough stock to serve e-voucher holders without delay, told farmers to protect their redemption codes, and pointed them to official weather advisories as a possible El Niño season approaches.

image.label: 675,459 redeemed
image.caption: Nearly two-thirds of the 1,024,434 farmers targeted by the 2026/27 FISP had collected their inputs by 23 October, the Ministry of Agriculture says.

body: Input redemption under this season's Farmer Input Support Programme is running ahead of last year, the Ministry of Agriculture said at the weekend. In a statement issued on Saturday 24 October by its principal public relations officer, Balewa Zyuulu, and reported by Zambia Monitor and News Diggers, the ministry said that as of Friday 23 October 675,459 farmers had redeemed their inputs under the 2026/27 programme. That is 65.93 per cent of the 1,024,434 beneficiaries targeted, and the ministry described redemption as significantly ahead of the pace recorded at the same point in 2025. News Diggers quoted the statement as saying implementation was progressing smoothly.

The statement's main purpose, as Zambia Monitor reported it, was a message to agro-dealers. The ministry urged dealers across the country to maintain adequate stocks of inputs so that farmers arriving to redeem e-vouchers are served without delay, calling sufficient stock critical to timely redemption as the planting season approaches. Farmers who have not yet redeemed were told to do so through accredited agro-dealers in good time, to obtain inputs only from accredited dealers, and to keep their e-voucher redemption codes to themselves.

body.text: Planting into an El Niño forecast

body: Zyuulu also tied the programme to the weather outlook. The statement encouraged farmers to follow official forecasts and seasonal advisories, and to consult extension officers on suitable crop varieties and climate-smart practices, given that an El Niño season could bring dry spells to parts of the country. Lusaka Brief reported on Sunday 25 October on the Government's El Niño preparedness plan and the Vice-President's warning that about 1.25 million people in 93 districts could face acute food insecurity in the lean season.

The ministry framed timely access to inputs as part of the Grow Zambia Agenda, which it said aims to raise agricultural production and productivity, strengthen food security, expand exports and improve farmers' livelihoods, and said it would continue to monitor the programme and provide guidance throughout the 2026/27 season.

The programme's cost is already visible in Parliament's in-tray. The second supplementary budget for 2026 presented by Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane last week includes K1.1 billion for the 2026/27 FISP e-voucher scheme within a K15.8 billion allocation to the Ministry of Agriculture, the Zambia Daily Mail reported; the far larger share of that allocation, K14.7 billion, is to pay farmers for the 2.7 million tonnes of maize the Food Reserve Agency bought this year against a target of 500,000 tonnes.

stories.title: Paid after death: the Auditor-General finds 77 deceased Ministry of Health workers were kept on the payroll for up to a year, at a cost of K5.79 million
stories.excerpt: The Auditor-General's report for 2025 says 77 health workers who had died remained on the Ministry of Health payroll for between one and twelve months, producing K5,790,691 in irregular payments, News Diggers and the Zambian Observer report. The same report found 63 officers past the retirement age of 60 still in service and paid K3.67 million, and 80 officers paid K1.16 million while unconfirmed in acting posts for up to 84 months. Who received the salaries of the dead is not stated.

image.label: 77 names, K5.79 million
image.caption: The Auditor-General's report for 2025 found deceased, over-age and unconfirmed officers on the Ministry of Health payroll.

body: The Auditor-General's report on the accounts for 2025 has produced a new finding about the Ministry of Health's payroll. According to News Diggers, which reported the detail on Sunday 25 October, 77 health workers who had died stayed on the ministry's payroll for up to twelve months after their deaths, and the salaries paid in that time, K5,790,691, are classed by the Auditor-General as irregular expenditure.

The Zambian Observer, reporting the same section of the report on Friday 23 October, broke the figure down: K5.71 million related to 76 deceased officers in Lusaka, and a single officer at ministry headquarters accounted for K75,721. The Observer noted that public service rules allow salary payments to stop when an officer dies, and that the report does not say who received the money paid in the names of the dead.

body.text: Past retirement, and never confirmed

body: The payroll findings go beyond the deceased. News Diggers reported that 63 officers who had passed the normal retirement age of 60 remained in active service and were paid salaries totalling K3,669,122, and that 80 Ministry of Health officers received K1,156,552 in salaries while still unconfirmed in their posts as at 31 August 2026, despite having served in acting positions for between three and 84 months. The report cites section 25(b)(i) of the 2023 Terms and Conditions of Service for the Public Service on the confirmation of officers.

The findings sit alongside the larger figure the report attaches to the health sector. Zambia Monitor's round-up of the week, published on Saturday 24 October, lists the Auditor-General's K3.56 billion in outstanding health sector obligations among its top stories, together with unaccounted-for confiscated mukula logs and weak revenue collection in government institutions. Lusaka Brief reported the K3.56 billion figure and the uncollected mining penalties on Wednesday 21 October.

None of the pages read carried a response from the Ministry of Health to the payroll findings, and the report, as summarised by the two outlets, does not say whether any of the money has been recovered or whether anyone has been disciplined. The Auditor-General's reports are tabled in the National Assembly and examined by the Public Accounts Committee, which is where controlling officers are normally called to answer for such findings.

stories.title: 'Incompetently before the court': the Attorney-General says Mukandila should have appealed to the Minister before asking the High Court to restore his NRC and passport
stories.excerpt: The State has asked the Lusaka High Court to throw out Celestine Mukandila's application for judicial review of the Gazette notice that cancelled his national registration card and passport. Attorney-General Mulilo Kabesha argues that the Tonse Alliance secretary-general should first have appealed to the Minister of Home Affairs and that judicial review is no shortcut around a statutory appeal, Zambia Monitor and News Diggers report. Mukandila says the Act gives no power to cancel an NRC by Gazette notice, and that he had no notice, hearing or reasons.

image.label: Gazette Notice 1418
image.caption: The Attorney-General argues that the challenge to the cancellation of Celestine Mukandila's documents should have gone to the Minister first.

body: The fight over Celestine Mukandila's citizenship has reached a procedural fork. In arguments filed in the Lusaka High Court and reported by Zambia Monitor on Saturday 24 October and by News Diggers on Friday 23 October, Attorney-General Mulilo Kabesha asked the court to dismiss, with costs, Mukandila's application for leave to begin judicial review of the Government's cancellation of his national registration card and passport.

The documents were cancelled by Government Gazette Notice No. 1418 of 2026, dated 2 September and issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal Security, on grounds of alleged fraud, false declaration or misrepresentation, according to Zambia Monitor. The State's position is that the matter is incompetently before the High Court: Mukandila, it argues, should first have appealed to the relevant Minister or Permanent Secretary, the court's unlimited original jurisdiction does not allow a litigant to bypass a procedure set by statute, and judicial review cannot be used to avoid a statutory appeal without exceptional circumstances.

body.text: Mukandila's case

body: Mukandila, the secretary-general of the Tonse Alliance and a legal practitioner, says he is a Zambian citizen by descent through his Zambian mother, although he was born in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Zambia Monitor reported that his citizenship was recognised by the Zambian Consulate General in Lubumbashi in 1999 and by the National Registration Office in 2017, and that he argues the cancellation was unlawful because he was given no prior notice, no hearing and no written reasons. His central legal point is that the National Registration Act, Chapter 126 of the Laws of Zambia, does not permit an NRC to be cancelled administratively by Gazette notice. He asks for leave to proceed and for a stay of the notice while the case is decided.

The detail of his account is in his affidavit, as summarised by Zambia Monitor when the case was filed on 11 September: born in Lubumbashi on 20 February 1990 while his grandfather was on a diplomatic posting, his late mother a Zambian from Mansa District, the family's return to Zambia in 1999, registration with the National Registration Office in 2006 at the age of 16, and a 2017 query about his NRC while he worked at the Road Transport and Safety Agency that, he says, ended with a letter confirming the card was authentic. He seeks orders of certiorari to quash the notice, mandamus to restore his documents and a declaration that he is a citizen by descent.

body.text: How the case got here

body: News Diggers reported on 26 September that the High Court had stayed the cancellation of the NRC and passport and that Mukandila, who had been arrested by the Department of Immigration in August after a report about his status, had been released on constitutional bail, according to his lawyer, Patrick Chulu. Zambia Monitor described him as detained when the application was filed.

body.confirmed: That Gazette Notice No. 1418 of 2026 cancelled Mukandila's NRC and passport, that he has applied for leave for judicial review in the Lusaka High Court, and that the Attorney-General has asked for the application to be dismissed on the ground that a statutory appeal should have come first, is reported by both Zambia Monitor and News Diggers.
body.unverified: The Government's allegation of fraud, false declaration or misrepresentation is untested; Mukandila denies it and says his citizenship was previously recognised. Neither outlet names the judge, gives the date of the ruling on leave, or reports whether the September stay remains in force pending that ruling.

stories.title: Lumezi's council chairperson in custody: police detain NRPUP's Dawson Tembo over an alleged trespass and a damaged door, four days after the complaint was lodged
stories.excerpt: Police in Eastern Province have detained Dawson Tembo, the NRPUP chairperson of Lumezi Town Council, on allegations of trespass and malicious damage to property, News Diggers and the Zambian Observer report. A 20-year-old woman from a village under Chief Zumwanda complained on 19 October that he had entered her premises and damaged her door; police say he evaded arrest until Friday 23 October. He is expected in court and the allegations have not been tested; no response from Tembo or his party has been reported.

image.label: Lumezi Town Council
image.caption: The chairperson of Lumezi Town Council was detained on Friday 23 October over a complaint of trespass and malicious damage.

body: The chairperson of Lumezi Town Council has spent the weekend in police custody. Dawson Tembo, who holds the post for the NRPUP, was detained on Friday 23 October on allegations of trespass and malicious damage to property, Eastern Province's police chief, Robertson Mweemba, confirmed in an interview on Saturday reported by News Diggers. The Zambian Observer carried a Zambia Reports account of the same detention.

The complaint was lodged at Lumezi Police Post on Monday 19 October by a 20-year-old woman from Kapilitiwa village under Chief Zumwanda, who alleged that Tembo had trespassed at her house and damaged the door. Lusaka Brief is not naming her. According to Mweemba, Tembo went into hiding after the complaint and was apprehended four days later; News Diggers quoted him as saying the chairperson was picked up on 23 October after being enticed. The Zambian Observer gave Tembo's age as 56 and his home as Mpeta village in Lumezi District.

body.text: A new office-holder

body: Tembo is a recent arrival in local government. News Diggers reported that he was sworn in as NRPUP council chairperson for Lumezi Town Council on 10 September, after the August general election. The Zambian Observer expands the party's initials as the New Revolution Party United Progressive.

Police told the Zambian Observer that Tembo is expected to appear in court. Neither outlet reported what led to the alleged confrontation, and the Observer's report noted explicitly that the allegations have yet to be tested in court. Nothing in the pages read records a response from Tembo himself, his lawyers or the NRPUP, and nothing suggests that he has yet been charged before a magistrate.

body.confirmed: That Dawson Tembo, Lumezi Town Council chairperson, was detained by police on Friday 23 October on allegations of trespass and malicious damage to property following a complaint lodged on 19 October is reported by News Diggers and the Zambian Observer, both citing Eastern Province police chief Robertson Mweemba.
body.unverified: The allegations are untested in court. The two outlets give Mweemba's title differently, as commanding officer and as commissioner. No charge sheet, court date, or statement from Tembo or the NRPUP had been reported by Sunday 25 October.

Police detain NRPUP council chairperson over damaged house door

stories.title: Nkana's run ends at Konkola: Blades win 2–0, Green Buffaloes come from behind in Kabwe and Chirundu win again, a day after Green Eagles dropped their first points
stories.excerpt: Week five of the MTN Super League transitional season closed on Sunday 25 October with Konkola Blades ending Nkana's three-match winning run 2–0 through Emmanuel Kunda and Idriss Ilunga Mbombo, Green Buffaloes beating Kabwe Warriors 2–1 away and Chirundu United winning 1–0 at Mufulira Wanderers, ZamFoot reports. On Saturday Green Eagles were held 0–0 by Nkwazi, their first dropped points, leaving Perry Mutapa's side top of Stream B on 10 points from four games.

image.label: Blades 2–0 Nkana
image.caption: Konkola Blades ended Nkana's winning run on Sunday 25 October as week five of the transitional Super League season closed.

body: Nkana's three-match winning run in the transitional MTN Super League season ended on Sunday 25 October at Konkola Stadium, where Konkola Blades beat the Kitwe side 2–0. ZamFoot reported that Emmanuel Kunda put Blades ahead in the 34th minute and that Idriss Ilunga Mbombo doubled the lead three minutes after the restart with a speculative effort. Nkana coach Elijah Tana had said before the match that his side were ready for Blades, ZamFoot reported on Saturday.

In Kabwe, Green Buffaloes came away with a 2–1 win over Kabwe Warriors. Paul Mbuyi headed the army side in front in the 65th minute and Golden Mashata chipped the goalkeeper for the second in the 74th; Charles Majapa Mumba's free-kick in the 90th minute came too late for Warriors. Chirundu United took their second win in a row with a 1–0 victory at Mufulira Wanderers, Andrew Simumba scoring from a free-kick in the 27th minute.

body.text: Eagles held, and happy with a point

body: The weekend's Stream B leaders had already played. On Saturday 24 October Green Eagles were held 0–0 by Nkwazi, their first dropped points of the campaign, and remain top of Stream B on 10 points from four matches, ZamFoot reported. Head coach Perry Mutapa said Nkwazi had started the stronger but that his side had the better chances late on, and Nkwazi goalkeeper Mangani Banda denied Eagles a late winner. Mutapa called it two points dropped, but added that at this stadium a point was acceptable, and praised the impact of his substitutes. Eagles' next opponents are Kabwe Warriors.

body.text: Going towards the end, I think we were the team with more chances to win, so I will say two points dropped.
body.attribution: Perry Mutapa, Green Eagles head coach, after the 0–0 draw with Nkwazi on Saturday 24 October, as reported by ZamFoot

body: Saturday's other results, reported by Lusaka Brief on Sunday 25 October, had FC MUZA beating champions Power Dynamos 1–0 to lead Stream A, with big wins for Trident, Zanaco and ZESCO United. ZamFoot's Sunday report did not publish updated standings for the transitional season.

Kabwe Warriors 1–2 Green Buffaloes (Mumba 90'; Mbuyi 65', Mashata 74')

stories.title: 'I expected nothing less than victory': the Air Force commander meets Red Arrows at the airport, sets a CAF final as the next target and hands coach Chisi Mbewe a car
stories.excerpt: Red Arrows came home from Durban to a late-night reception at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport led by Zambia Air Force commander Lieutenant General Oscar Nyoni, who told the players their first CAF Confederation Cup group place should be the start of a push for the final, ZamFoot reports. Nyoni, the club's patron, presented head coach Chisi Mbewe with a Toyota Mark X, and FAZ's delegation leader Samuel Mwape called the qualification a milestone for Zambian football.

image.label: Arrows come home
image.caption: Red Arrows were received at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport by the Zambia Air Force commander after beating Kaizer Chiefs on penalties.

body: The Zambia Air Force gave its football club a commander's welcome. Red Arrows, who beat Kaizer Chiefs on penalties in Durban on Friday 23 October to reach the CAF Confederation Cup group stage for the first time, were received at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport at 21:30 by the Air Force commander, Lieutenant General Oscar Nyoni, ZamFoot reported on Sunday 25 October.

Nyoni, who is also the club's patron, told the squad he had come in person to keep a promise made before the tie. He said the win deserved celebration but should serve as motivation for greater achievement, and set the target as a place in the competition's final.

body.text: I expected nothing less than victory and you have brought that victory. Congratulations.
body.attribution: Lieutenant General Oscar Nyoni, Zambia Air Force commander and Red Arrows patron, receiving the team at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport, as reported by ZamFoot

body: The commander presented head coach Chisi Mbewe with a Toyota Mark X, which ZamFoot said was to help him travel to training and on official duties. ZamFoot also reported that President Hakainde Hichilema had praised the victory, which it described as adding to the pride of the Air Force.

body.text: 'A significant milestone'

body: Brigadier General Simon Tembo, who led the Air Force delegation to Durban, described Arrows as a disciplined, quality side. Samuel Mwape, the Football Association of Zambia's representative and overall leader of the delegation, congratulated the club and called its qualification a significant milestone for Zambian football. He asked Nyoni to keep backing the team and said FAZ was open to working with the Air Force on football development.

Arrows' place in the group stage was secured over two legs that ended level and went to a shoot-out at the Moses Mabhida Stadium. Lusaka Brief reported the match on Sunday 25 October: a 1–0 defeat in Durban that levelled the tie, followed by a 3–2 win on penalties. The group-stage draw had not been reported in the pages read for this edition.

analysis.title: Friday's budget arrives with this year's maize bill already on the table
analysis.body: The 2027 budget on Friday 30 October will be read against two documents from the past week. The first is the K19.9 billion supplementary request for 2026, three-quarters of it to pay farmers for maize the Food Reserve Agency bought far beyond its target: 2.7 million tonnes against 500,000. Most of that is to be financed by K18 billion of domestic borrowing. The second is the World Bank's pledge to back the 2027 fiscal programme through a Development Policy Operation. Between them they define the question for the Finance Minister: how a budget that must absorb the cost of a bumper harvest, and fund an El Niño lean season the Vice-President has already put a number on, stays within a programme that lenders will support. What to watch: the size of the domestic borrowing requirement, whether FISP and FRA are budgeted at this year's realised cost or at last year's plan, and what the ten working days of sector scrutiny do to the estimates before the House resumes on 24 November. The case for optimism is that the harvest and input redemption are ahead of schedule; the case for caution is that both are expensive.

analysis.title: The 48-hour rule is becoming the opposition's yardstick for the new term
analysis.body: Fred M'membe's Sunday statement and Cornelius Mweetwa's Thursday speech describe the same ten weeks and reach opposite conclusions. The Socialist Party's case rests on the Constitution's 48-hour limit on detention without charge or a court appearance, and on the cases now before the courts: the treason charges against Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others, and the Lima MP who sought bail after five days in custody. The State's answer, filed in the treason case, is that complex cases take time to investigate; the ruling party's broader answer, in Mweetwa's words, is that the election itself passed without violence except for the disorder that followed Mundubile's claim of victory. Both can be partly right. What the statement as reported did not do is list names, dates and durations, which is what would allow the claim of a pattern to be tested against the police's own records. What to watch: the rulings on bail and on the rights challenge in the treason case, whether any detention beyond 48 hours is explained in court, and how the police conduct the Mandevu campaign after the Inspector General's promise of impartial enforcement.

analysis.title: Mukandila's case turns on a procedural question before it reaches citizenship
analysis.body: The Attorney-General's argument is deliberately narrow. It does not yet engage with whether Celestine Mukandila is a citizen by descent, or whether his NRC was obtained by fraud; it says the High Court should not hear the question at all until the Minister of Home Affairs has, because the law provides an appeal and judicial review is not a shortcut around it. Mukandila's reply is equally structural: the National Registration Act, he says, gives nobody the power to cancel an NRC by Gazette notice, so there was no lawful decision to appeal against, only an act with no statutory basis, taken without notice, hearing or reasons. The State itself concedes, in the arguments reported, that exceptional circumstances can justify skipping a statutory appeal; Mukandila's claim that there was no power to cancel at all is an attempt to fit that exception. Which of the two framings the judge accepts will decide whether the case ends at leave or proceeds to the citizenship question. What to watch: the ruling on leave, whether the September stay survives it, and, if the case proceeds, what evidence the State offers for the fraud allegation that the Gazette notice asserts and Mukandila denies.
